turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Sam Whitfield. I have fifteen minutes, go ahead.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Thanks, Sam. I’ll keep it brief: how much manager time goes into call coaching today, and where are they still flying blind?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I don’t have a clean number on manager coaching time. Why is this worth forty-eight thousand dollars?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Fair question: it gives every rep realistic practice and managers quote-backed scoring, so coaching targets gaps earlier. What does delayed ramp or missed quota cost?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: A new rep costs us about ninety thousand dollars a year fully loaded. How many weeks of ramp will you remove, and can you get the price down to thirty-five thousand?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: I can’t credibly promise weeks yet. Let’s review current ramp data and pilot results; at $35k, we’d need to trade scope or terms.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Forty-eight is outside budget without a quantified ramp impact. What scope or terms get us to thirty-five, and what date do you propose for a business-case review with our VP of Sales?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: At $35k, I’d scope to 30 reps with annual prepayment. Could we review ramp assumptions and pilot criteria with your VP on November 3?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: November 3 works. Thirty-five thousand for 30 reps doesn’t meet the requirement; can you cover all 40 with annual prepayment and bring a model showing ramp weeks saved and dollar impact?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: I can take $35k for all 40 forward with annual prepayment, contingent on the business case. I’ll bring the ramp-impact model November 3.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Good. Include the baseline ramp, expected weeks saved, and dollar impact at thirty-five thousand for all 40 reps. Send me the business case and we'll take it from there.
